description:
Store each issue's lease in its own file, published by the lease lock's apply, so reading or changing one lease reads only that file and an interruption leaves the prior or the next lease.

## Background

`LeaseLock` (`load`, `list`, `apply`) and the lock-free reads (`read_leases`, `read_active_leases`, `read_active_lease`) in `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs` are the only access to lease state. They store every lease in `claims.index.json` under `WorktreePaths::shared_jit` (`<common-dir>/jit`, named `.git/jit` below), rebuilt from `claims.jsonl` when the lock is taken, and take each sequence number by rescanning the log (`get_next_seq`, private). The index publish has a fixed temp name and no directory sync (`write_index_atomic`). `Lease.stale` is a stored field that the rebuild computes. The atomic-write primitives `write_file_synced`, `create_file_synced` and `sync_directory` (`storage/atomic_write.rs`) are visible to the storage module. `jit recover` verifies and rebuilds the index from the log until that machinery is deleted.

Kept as one change for a test reason: the shared test helper and the failure-lever expectations name the store's files, so the suites stay green only if they move with the store. The failure-lever registry expects `PARSE_ERROR: Failed to parse claims index` for a malformed store (`tests/cli_issue/failure_lever_registry.toml`).

The repository format is already 4 when this lands, and the installed binary stays at format 3 until the cutover window, so machine-local leases are not read by this code until the window rewrites them.

Absorbed from 53d19851: no lease operation reads the index or the log. What remains of the index model:

- `rebuild_index_from_log`, `rebuild_index_from_log_at`, `verify_index_consistency`, `write_index_atomic`, `evict_expired` and `load_claims_index` (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs`), with `ClaimsIndex` itself, `ClaimsIndex::warnings` and `ClaimsMutationGuard::warnings` and its caller in `commands/mod.rs`;
- `jit recover`'s verify-and-rebuild step (`commands/claim.rs`), its `index_rebuilt` report field (`main.rs`) and help text (`cli.rs`);
- `StorageWarning::SequenceGap`, `DuplicateLease` and `IndexRebuilt` (`storage/warnings.rs`);
- the rebuild property tests `prop_index_rebuild_idempotent`, `prop_no_data_loss_in_rebuild` and `prop_staleness_computed_during_rebuild`;
- the recovery tests in `tests/cli_repo_workflow/claim_integration_tests.rs` that remove the index, and `test_recover_empty_claim_log_does_not_warn_about_missing_index`, which reads `index_rebuilt`;
- repository validation's checks of the machine-local index (`validate_machine_local_claims`, `validation/repository.rs`; `validate_claims_index_at` and `validate_claims_index_with_paths`, `commands/validate.rs`, re-exported in `commands/mod.rs`) and `test_validate_repository_detects_invalid_claims_index` (`tests/cli_item_validate/validation_lease_tests.rs`).

`JIT_TEST_MODE` exists only to skip that validation check: `src/test_mode.rs` has one reader in `validation/repository.rs`. It is set by `src/test_cli.rs`, asserted by `tests/cli_repo_workflow/cli_process_fixture_tests.rs` and `tests/scratch_build/process_state_policy_tests.rs`, and described in `dev/TESTING.md`.

`jit recover`'s passes are redo completion at session open, derived-state repair, stale-lock cleanup, expired-lease eviction, stale indefinite-lease reclaim and temp-file cleanup.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each active lease is the file `.git/jit/leases/<issue-id>.json`, named by one path constructor on `WorktreePaths` built on `shared_jit`. An absent file means no lease, and `Lease.stale` no longer exists. `LeaseLock` and the lock-free reads read and write only these files, and neither reads or writes `claims.index.json` or reads `claims.jsonl`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `apply` publishes by synced temp file, rename and directory sync (or unlink and directory sync), then takes the next number from `.git/jit/claims.seq`, then appends the operation's history lines; `get_next_seq` no longer exists. Reading or changing one issue's lease reads only that file, and only the limit check and listing read the lease directory.
- [hard] REQ-03: `list()` and the lock-free reads treat only names of the form `<issue-id>.json` as lease records and skip every other name in the directory, such as an interrupted operation's stage file.
- [hard] REQ-04: The shared lease test helper plants, reads and corrupts lease records, and the failure levers expect a malformed lease record to fail `claim status` and `claim list` with `PARSE_ERROR` and exit 1.
- [hard] REQ-05: The listed functions, `ClaimsIndex`, both `warnings` methods, the three warnings, `RecoveryReport.index_rebuilt` and recovery's verify-and-rebuild step no longer exist; no command rebuilds lease state from the claims log, reads `claims.jsonl` or writes `claims.index.json`.
- [hard] REQ-06: `jit recover`'s help names exactly the passes listed in the Background.
- [hard] REQ-07: The rebuild property tests and the index-removal recovery tests no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-08: `validate_claims_index_at`, `validate_claims_index_with_paths`, `validate_machine_local_claims` and `test_validate_repository_detects_invalid_claims_index` no longer exist, repository validation reads nothing under `.git/jit/`, the remaining lease-validation tests pass, and no validation-report input carries claims-index problems.
- [hard] REQ-09: `src/test_mode.rs`, its module declaration and every mention of `JIT_TEST_MODE` in `crates/` and `dev/TESTING.md` no longer exist.

## Decisions

- D-1: Steward ruling (just-in-time-6a, 2026-11-04, for the user): 53d19851 is absorbed into this issue after code-review found the claims-index replay still live through recovery and validation; its criteria are REQ-05 to REQ-09 here, verbatim, and 53d19851 is rejected as merged-into-2f563673.
- D-2: Steward ruling (just-in-time-6a, 2026-11-04, for the user): the lease-directory scan in renew, heartbeat and force-evict (`find_by_lease_id`) is the plan's fixed contract `lease-id-scan-bridge`, accepted for this issue until 614a6f97 makes those commands issue-addressed. Every issue-addressed read and change still reads only that issue's file.
title: Each lease is one record under the lease lock
